writeup: TIC 469306687 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 6.17 percent and an orbital period of 2.3123 days, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 166.2 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a centroid offset of 2.8 arcseconds and a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 31.1. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unreported object. While the machine learning model assigns this target a moderate screening score of 0.31, the candidate passed all data quality checks and warrants further study to determine its true nature.
